newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Clal Israel Q4 loss 1.3 mln shekel.
newsitem.headline: Clal Israel Q4 loss 1.3 mln shekel.

text.p: Clal Israel.
(in thousands of shekels except EPS)
General Profits Loss-4,844 n/a 130,937 370,994
Insurance Profits 21,841 n/a 106,042 57,881
Net Loss-1,307 n/a Profit 111,600 203,761
Earnings per share n/a n/a 3.59 6.62
Note: General and insurance profits are after taxes.

Clal Israel said the 45 percent decline in full-year net and the fourth-quarter loss were due mainly to its Clal Industries unit. Attributable earnings from Clal Industries fell in the year to 52.2 million shekels from 174.3 million in 1995.
In addition, Clal Trading, which covers the group's retail and trading activities, saw attributable earnings fall to 1.1 million shekels from 18.5 million shekels in 1995.

The downturns were only partially offset by a near doubling in attributable profits from Clal Insurance Holdings to 73.3 million shekels and from property and building operations, where they grew to 44.2 million shekels from 33.4 million shekels.

Clal Israel, one of Israel's leading holding companies, said return on equity fell to 4.3 percent last year from 8.5 percent in 1995. The company has interests in high technology, industry, insurance, property development and commerce.
It said directors had approved an aggregate cash dividend of 40 million shekels.

Clal Israel said it had taken charges totalling 102.6 million shekels during 1996 mainly to write-downs on the value of its holdings in Scitex Corp., Sunfrost Ltd and Clal Trading among others. Many of these companies also reported losses or declines in profits, the company said.
The charges were partly offset by capital gains of 73.3 million shekels, Clal Israel said.
Discounting one-time factors, Clal Israel said, it nevertheless would have posted a decline in net profit to 141 million shekels last year from 166 million shekels in 1995.
Clal Israel's two top officers -- chairman Avi Olshansky and managing director David Wainshal -- are due to step down March 31 to be replaced respectively by Leon Recanati and Yitzhak Kaul.
($1 = 3.37 shekels)
